source_title: Revlon files for bankruptcy amid competition and supply chain stress
company_context: Revlon Inc., the legacy US cosmetics and personal-care manufacturer (SEC EDGAR CIK 0000887921), filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions on June 16, 2022 in the US Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York, weighed down by a large legacy debt load and acute liquidity strain from supply-chain disruption and inflation.
business_type: Consumer packaged goods / cosmetics manufacturing (inventory- and working-capital-intensive, global supply chain)
evidence_summary: Revlon and certain subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on June 16, 2022 carrying roughly $3.6-3.7 billion of debt. The proximate driver was liquidity stress: supply-chain disruption and rising inflation raised input costs and strained the company's ability to meet lender obligations on its legacy capital structure. Upon court approval the company expected to receive $575 million in debtor-in-possession financing from its existing lender base, which, together with its existing working-capital facility, was intended to fund day-to-day operations during reorganization.

source_backed_metrics.filing_court: US Bankruptcy Court, Southern District of New York

outcome_evidence: Filed Chapter 11 on June 16, 2022 with a $575 million DIP financing commitment to support operations during reorganization of its legacy capital structure amid supply-chain and inflation-driven liquidity constraints.
source_limitations: Named journalism summary; the underlying SEC 8-K and court petition were not fetched directly (SEC htm access-blocked). Debt stated as a range ($3.6-3.7 billion) across sources.
directly_stated: Filed Chapter 11 on June 16, 2022 in SDNY
$575 million DIP financing from existing lender base
Cited supply-chain disruption and inflation as drivers of liquidity constraints
inferred: Rising input costs compressed working-capital headroom faster than the legacy debt could be serviced
The capital structure left no liquidity cushion to absorb cost shocks
why_useful_for_opsiq: A manufacturing/CPG case where debt and working-capital stress combine: a legacy debt load plus a supply-chain/inflation cost shock tips a viable brand into Chapter 11. Useful for testing whether OpsIQ distinguishes working_capital_stress from pure debt_solvency_pressure, and for modeling adaptive re-evaluation when a cost/supply shock erodes liquidity.
